commands.review_summary:
The branch separates recoverable Discord tail handler failures from fatal tail failures, serializes ordered events, durably records timed-out or panicked message identities, and adds bounded exact-message replay through maintenance and a replay-only CLI mode.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current behavior routes event-scoped handler failures through the tail-ending path, and a missed message can become unreachable to forward repair once its cursor advances. The PR's focused regression tests exercise those paths, but this review did not establish a live current-main Discord reproduction.

target.title: fix: keep tail alive and replay timed-out messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Discord Gateway event handler error, recovered panic, or cooperative timeout
previously shared the same fatal path as worker-queue saturation. Keeping the
tail alive exposed a second loss mode: a timed-out message can remain absent
after the channel cursor advances beyond it, so ordinary forward repair can no
longer fetch that exact message.

The recovery path also needs to fail closed when an ordered handler ignores
cancellation. Otherwise the timed-out handler can continue writing while later
ordered events begin, and the exact failed message may not be durably recorded
before the tail exits.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Separate ordinary event-scoped failures from fatal tail failures while
  retaining bounded three-consecutive-failure escalation.
- Serialize message and channel events on one ordered worker while member work
  uses separate workers and a separate failure circuit.
- Treat a genuinely detached ordered timeout as immediately fatal, stop later
  ordered dequeue, and preserve that fatal result across concurrent shutdown.
- Persist the exact timed-out message identity transactionally before fatal
  return; surface persistence failures in the supervisor-visible error.
- Carry safe event metadata through queued work and reject conflicting
  identities returned by message-update refetches.
- Process bounded unresolved `discord/tail_message` failures through the
  maintenance-only replay path after ordinary forward repair.
- Fetch each replay candidate by exact channel/message ID, validate identity,
  and persist through the canonical idempotent message upsert path.
- Resolve the exact failure only after durable canonical presence. Missing,
  inaccessible, mismatched, and retryable responses remain unresolved.
- Keep replay guild-scoped, exclusion-aware, bounded, idempotent, and free of
  synthetic `message_events`, publishing, cursor regression, or
  `tail:last_event` updates.

## User Impact

Transient per-event failures no longer stop a healthy Gateway tail. A
non-cooperative ordered handler cannot overlap later ordered work, and its exact
message identity is durably retained before the supervisor restarts the tail.
Hourly maintenance can recover a failed message behind its channel cursor
without replaying channel history or duplicating Gateway events.

Warnings and replay summaries contain identifiers and classifications only;
they do not log message content, payloads, usernames, tokens, panic values, or
raw secret-bearing errors.

## Evidence

Current head: `c3e236905f6a4ef4ea05d6c4303340ee24630fb0`

- `go test -count=1 ./...`
- Filtered repository coverage: `85.1%` against the `85.0%` floor
- `go test -count=1 -race ./...`
- Focused timeout boundary tests: 50 normal and 20 race repetitions
- `go vet ./...`
- `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `deadcode`, `gofumpt`, and `gosec`
- `govulncheck ./...`
- Build and CLI control-surface smoke checks
- Independent Pinchy review: `ZERO BLOCKERS`

Focused tests cover detached-timeout ordering, durable failure persistence,
recorder failure, parent-shutdown races, cancellation-grace boundaries,
below-cursor recovery, monotonic cursors, idempotence, no synthetic events,
unchanged `tail:last_event`, bounded retry rotation, guild scope, channel
exclusions, normal-page resolution, inaccessible responses, and identity
mismatches.
